purpose: Single machine-readable registry of the sources that a GitHub Pages deployment builds or ships. It drives scripts/validate_deployment.mjs and is the only place where deployment roles, expected spatial scope and integrity guardrails are declared. It deliberately contains no individual map records.
guardrail_note: Every min_count in this file is an ENGINEERING guardrail against an ingestion collapse (a truncated download, a schema change, an upstream outage that still returns parseable JSON). It is not a tourism indicator, not a threshold with analytical meaning, and not a claim about how many museums, stations or hotels Madrid has. Each value is set far below the count actually observed at calibration so that legitimate source change passes and only an obvious collapse fails. baseline_count and calibrated_on are recorded so a reviewer can see the headroom; changing a min_count is a visible diff and must be justified in the pull request that changes it.

madrid_city_area.note: Generous box around the municipality of Madrid. Deliberately loose: its job is to catch null-island coordinates, swapped lat/lon, projected coordinates leaking through unconverted, and a source returning a different city — not to assert an administrative boundary.

central_madrid_area.note: Generous box around the app's central-Madrid envelope (40.385-40.455 N, -3.745 to -3.645 E). Looser than the envelope on purpose: the CRTM station query uses esriSpatialRelIntersects, so a station sitting on the boundary can be returned marginally outside it (observed: Plaza Eliptica at 40.38460, ~44 m outside). A strict envelope check would fail a healthy build.

madrid_city_and_surroundings_feed_area.note: INTEGRITY ENVELOPE ONLY for the Madrid Destino / esmadrid accommodation feed - not a statement of coverage. The dataset is published as 'Alojamientos de la ciudad de Madrid' and its specification describes the content as accommodation of 'la ciudad de Madrid y alrededores' (the city of Madrid and its surroundings). The box is deliberately loose so that a record in the surroundings does not fail the build, while a null-island coordinate, a swapped lat/lon or a different country still does. On 2026-09-29, 4 of 613 records fell outside the municipality, the furthest at 40.711 N / -3.994 E; those records are reported as a manifest warning against madrid_city_area and are deliberately NOT filtered here, because narrowing the layer would be an analytical semantics change rather than an integrity fix.
madrid_city_and_surroundings_feed_area.not_a_regional_dataset: This envelope must never be read as Comunidad de Madrid coverage. This feed is a city-and-surroundings accommodation register, not a regional one. A future Comunidad de Madrid level requires its own authoritative regional datasets and must not inherit this feed as a proxy for them.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Madrid Open Data
sources.source_period_semantics: State of the municipal register at the moment of retrieval. The resource publishes no period or edition field, so no source period is recorded for this layer.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~37% of the observed count. A municipal museum register cannot plausibly fall to a quarter of its size; below this, assume a truncated or changed response.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: A count of register entries, not a measure of cultural provision, visitor numbers or attractiveness. Not an exhaustive inventory of cultural supply in Madrid.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Madrid Open Data
sources.source_period_semantics: State of the municipal register at the moment of retrieval. No period field is published.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: This layer is small, so a ratio is statistically meaningless; an absolute floor is used instead. Fewer than four official tourist information points city-wide would indicate a broken response rather than a municipal decision.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Presence of official information points. Not service hours, staffing, languages offered or quality.

sources.source_period_semantics: Station network as published at the moment of retrieval. The station GeoJSON carries no period field.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~40% of the observed count. Tolerates real network contraction and station rebuilds; catches a truncated feed.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Station presence only. Not dock capacity, bike availability, service level or accessibility.

sources.authority: Consorcio Regional de Transportes de Madrid (CRTM) open data
sources.source_period_semantics: Station layers as served by the CRTM feature services at the moment of retrieval.

required_modes.note: This layer merges two independent feature services (M4 Metro, M5 Cercanias). A combined count can stay healthy while one mode silently disappears, so each mode is checked separately.

metro.rationale: ~36% of the observed Metro count inside the query envelope.

cercanias.rationale: Only a handful of Cercanias stations fall inside the central envelope, so an absolute floor is used. Zero Cercanias records means the M5 service failed.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~40% of the observed combined count, in addition to the per-mode floors above.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Infrastructure presence. Not service frequency, capacity, step-free access or connectivity. Metro and Cercanias records at the same interchange are not deduplicated, and a station with several access points may appear more than once.

sources.source_period_semantics: Catalogue state at the moment of retrieval. The XML feed publishes no edition or effective date.

authoritative_builder.note: Guards the owner ruling that the Madrid Destino / esMADRID published catalogue remains the canonical source for this operational accommodation layer. A deployment artifact whose accommodation layer was produced by the browser's OpenStreetMap/Overpass fallback must not be published as if it came from the Madrid Destino catalogue. This check inspects the artifact only; the browser-side runtime fallback in js/data.js is a separate behaviour change and is untouched here.

taxonomy.note: Observed on 2026-09-29: 610/613 records carried a source category and 3/613 fell to 'other'. These broad ratios catch the taxonomy block disappearing from the feed or a parser change that collapses every record to unclassified, without asserting a particular category distribution.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~41% of the observed count. Tolerates real catalogue churn; catches a truncated XML parse.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Accommodation listings curated and published by Madrid Destino / esMADRID, taken as a deployment snapshot of the published XML catalogue and counted one per listing. This is a tourism-promotion catalogue, NOT a complete administrative register of accommodation. It is NOT accommodation capacity, beds, places or rooms (a 300-room hotel and a 4-room pension each count as one); NOT occupancy, price or legal status; NOT the complete municipal accommodation stock and NOT regional stock. Its catalogue universe is heterogeneous and includes objects such as university residences and campsites. Published as 'Alojamientos de la ciudad de Madrid', covering the city of Madrid and its surroundings, so it is neither a strictly municipal register nor a Comunidad de Madrid one, and must not be used as a regional dataset. See docs/ACCOMMODATION_NUMERATOR_AUDIT.md (Gate A).

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Madrid Open Data
sources.source_period_semantics: State of the municipal register at the moment of retrieval.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~35% of the observed count. Reported as a warning, not a failure: this layer is cartographic context, is excluded from every lens metric in code, and the app already disables its toggle and reports it unavailable when absent.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Map context only. Never a numerator or denominator. Not shade, cooling, thermal comfort, biodiversity, accessibility, quality or attractiveness, and not a complete inventory of Madrid green space.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Madrid Open Data
sources.source_period_semantics: The published counter records carry their own dates, so this layer's source period is derived from the observed date bounds of the records themselves. It is never taken from the build timestamp. The latest published quarter may be provisional.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: ~33% of the observed station count, reported as a warning. Volume change in an optional opt-in evidence layer does not justify withholding the whole site; internal incoherence does, and is checked separately as a hard failure.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Observed pedestrians passing fixed municipal counters during the published period. NOT tourists, tourist flow, visitor demand, crowding, carrying capacity or current conditions. No value exists between counters.

sources.source_period_semantics: One modelled pilot day, 21 August 2023, at three modelled times of day. Fixed by the source; never derived from the build timestamp.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: This artifact is committed and locked, not fetched at deploy time, so it can only change through a commit. The floor equals the baseline exactly: the bounded pilot is 14 outdoor assets and any change to that number is a deliberate evidence-boundary change that must not reach a deployment unnoticed.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: Model-derived (SOLWEIG) UTCI at 14 sampled outdoor points on one historical day. Not measured comfort, not current conditions, not a city-wide surface, and never to be interpolated between sample points.

sources.authority: MIXED - curated in this repository from several different upstream sources, which are NOT the same set of authorities the deployment sources use. Per-layer provenance is recorded in data/snapshot_provenance.json and is the authoritative description of where each fallback record came from. Notably the accommodation records in this sample are OpenStreetMap-derived (ODbL, via Overpass), not Madrid Destino / esmadrid records.
sources.source_period_semantics: Capture dates are recorded per layer in data/snapshot_provenance.json. This is a sample, not an edition of any source, and it has no source period of its own.

integrity_guardrail.rationale: Committed last-resort fallback (4 museums, 2 information points, 6 accommodation records). Checked for presence and coordinate sanity so the fallback path cannot silently become empty.

sources.interpretation_ceiling: A deliberately small, non-exhaustive curated sample, never a complete inventory: a count from this layer means 'records present in this sample', not 'records that exist at this location'. It carries the separate SNAPSHOT SAMPLE evidence state in the UI and must never be presented as current authoritative Madrid evidence. In particular its accommodation records are OpenStreetMap-derived and are NOT official Madrid Destino accommodation evidence; they must not be read as the authoritative accommodation register, and no count from them may be compared with a deployment-snapshot accommodation count. Retiring this OpenStreetMap-derived accommodation fallback is a separate, separately-reviewable behaviour change.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - IDEAM (Infraestructura de Datos Espaciales del Ayuntamiento de Madrid)
sources.source_period_semantics: No effective or edition date of the geometry is published, so this geography has no source period; source_period is null and source_period_known is false. What the authority does publish is a dataset version ('Versión de los datos'): district v3.2.1 and barrio v3.4.1 at capture, recorded in geography/madrid_admin.meta.json under source_version.datasets[*].published_version. The CKAN catalogue's metadata-modified date is recorded there too, as catalog_metadata_modified, and is ONLY the catalogue record's modification date - it is not the geometry's edition or vintage and must never be presented as one. The builder's retrieval/build time is recorded separately as retrieved_at. A future join should cite the published version (e.g. 'Padron period X joined to Madrid barrio geography v3.4.1'), never a catalogue timestamp. The geography is committed, not fetched at deploy time (rebuilt_at_deploy is false), and administrative boundaries are never made to look fresh because the builder ran.

expected_counts.note: Verified against the authority on 2026-09-29: 21 districts and 131 barrios. A change to these counts is a deliberate change to Madrid's administrative division and must not reach a deployment unnoticed.

sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature: the application now resolves each Lens centre to its official barrio and district at runtime and names that place in the interface, so this artifact is consumed by a user-facing feature. A deployment must not publish an Area Profile experience backed by a missing, truncated or incoherent administrative geography, because the failure mode is a confident wrong place name rather than a visibly empty panel. The Node and Python test suites still enforce the same structural contract on every push; this gate is the second line, at publication.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Administrative reference geography for spatial joins and containment only. It is a common join target for future datasets (Padron, accommodation, VUT, restaurants, housing, socioeconomic and environmental indicators), not an analytical metric and not a denominator on its own. The municipality polygon is DERIVED as the union of the 21 official district polygons and is flagged as such. Administrative-area statistics must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens or any sub-area; a Lens may report the official barrio/district containing a point, kept clearly separate from circle-derived measurements. This municipal geography is not Comunidad de Madrid geography.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Subdireccion General de Estadistica (Padron Municipal de habitantes)
sources.source_period_semantics: The population period is the source reference date, published as '1 de enero de <year>' (a real Padron reference date), recorded in population/madrid_population.json under source_period.reference_date and echoed in the sidecar meta. It is source-derived and never taken from the build clock; the builder's retrieval/build time is recorded separately as retrieved_at in the meta. The selected period is the latest annual reference date whose barrio coverage exactly matches the canonical geography, so a year with partial coverage is treated as incomplete rather than as the latest. The geography version this joins against (barrio v3.4.1 / district v3.2.1) is recorded in the meta under geography_linkage and is distinct from the population period: an audit can state 'population period X joined to Madrid barrio geography v3.4.1'.

expected_counts.note: Every canonical barrio must have exactly one resident count for the selected period; district and municipality totals are derived from the barrios. A change to these counts is a change to the canonical join universe and must not reach a deployment unnoticed.

sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature: the application now reads the registered-resident figure of the barrio containing a Lens centre and shows it, with its reference date, in the interface. A deployment must not publish a resident count that is missing, mis-joined or detached from its period. The UI abstains rather than showing a zero when a figure is absent, but an artifact that is broken at build time must not reach the public site at all. The Node and Python test suites still enforce the same contract on every push.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Persons registered in the municipal Padron for the reference date. This is a residential denominator only: it is NOT people physically present at a given moment, NOT daytime population, NOT tourists, NOT workers present, NOT unique mobile-device users, NOT households and NOT housing units. This PR defines no tourism indicator, no accommodation-per-resident or hotels-per-1000 ratio, no tourism pressure and no composite score. A barrio population belongs to the whole official barrio and must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens; a Lens may state 'the centre is in barrio X, which has Y registered residents for period Z', where Y remains a barrio statistic, not the population inside the circle. This municipal population is not Comunidad de Madrid population.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Agencia de Actividades, Subdireccion General de Actividades Economicas, Servicio de Licencias y Consultas
sources.source_period_semantics: The source declares NO reference date and NO effective date, so this layer has no source period: source_period is null and source_period_known is false. Four different dates exist around this artifact and are never collapsed into one. (1) The HTTP Last-Modified header observed on the resource file when the builder fetched it (Mon, 07 Sep 2026 10:11:03 GMT), recorded in the artifact under source_state.xlsx_http_last_modified. It describes the state of the FILE SERVED and is NOT a publisher-declared publication, effective or reference date; it must never be presented as one, and the interface says 'source file state', never 'reference'. (2) The span of per-record licence grant dates present in the extract (2019-03-06 to 2026-09-02), which is a property of the records, not of the publication. (3) The portal catalogue's own metadata date. (4) The builder's retrieved_at clock. The residential denominator's reference date (1 January 2026) belongs to a DIFFERENT source with different temporal semantics and the two are never shown as one shared period.

count_fields.note: COUNT of distinct EXPEDIENTE_LU and SUM of the source column 'N VUT' respectively. A licence is not a dwelling: in the audited extract one licence covered 48 units, so vut_units >= vut_licences must hold for every record and the two are never given each other's name. The user-facing primary quantity is vut_units.

expected_counts.note: Every canonical barrio must carry exactly one pair of counts for this source snapshot; district and municipality totals are derived from the barrios. A change to these counts is a change to the canonical join universe and must not reach a deployment unnoticed.

expected_source_totals.note: The totals of THIS COMMITTED SNAPSHOT, pinned so an accidental or partial regeneration is a visible diff rather than a silent one. They are not eternal source truths: the upstream dataset is updated bimonthly, and a deliberate refresh re-runs scripts/build_vut_licence_numerator.py and updates these numbers in the same reviewed pull request as the artifact. The builder derives them from the source and never reads them from here.

sources.zero_semantics: Scoped to this source extract only. The extract enumerates granted activity-licence records across the whole municipality, so a barrio with no matched record carries zero published granted licences and zero source-reported units rather than missing data. This is the one documented exception to this project's 'missing is not zero' rule. A zero is NOT an assertion that no tourist-dwelling activity has ever existed or exists today in that barrio, and a failure to load or validate this artifact must never be degraded into a zero: the interface abstains instead.
sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING since the Area Profile feature began showing licensed VUT context: the application reads the licensed-VUT figures of the barrio containing a Lens centre and displays them, with a descriptive per-1,000-registered-residents ratio, in the interface. A deployment must not publish an administrative indicator that is missing, mis-joined, numerically incoherent or detached from its provenance, because the failure mode is a confident wrong number - or a plausible-looking zero - rather than a visibly empty panel. The browser degrades gracefully when a runtime fetch fails and shows the licensed-VUT block as unavailable; that is a separate concern from this gate, which verifies the COMMITTED artifact at publication time. The Node and Python suites enforce the same contract on every push.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED ADMINISTRATIVE SNAPSHOT. This artifact is not rebuilt during the Pages deployment (rebuilt_at_deploy is false): deployment validation verifies the committed file, and a successful deployment therefore does NOT mean the upstream source was re-fetched at deploy time. Refreshing it requires explicitly re-running scripts/build_vut_licence_numerator.py and reviewing the diff, including the pinned expected_source_totals above. Nothing about this layer is live data.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: A count of urban-planning activity licences GRANTED for tourist-dwelling (vivienda de uso turistico) use in the city of Madrid, and of the tourist-dwelling units those licences include. The primary quantity is units; the licence count is supporting evidence and a licence is NOT a dwelling. It does NOT establish that the dwellings are currently operating: the source carries no revocation, expiry or cessation field and publishes no retention policy, so nothing may call these 'active', 'operating' or 'current' tourist dwellings, and the extract is not described as a cumulative stock. It is NOT all VUT (it excludes responsible declarations filed with the Comunidad de Madrid and the regional inventory), NOT all accommodation (the publisher names tourist apartments, hostels, guest houses, hotels, pensions and aparthotels as excluded), NOT beds, rooms or places, NOT platform listings and NOT evidence of the legality of any platform listing. It is NOT a measure of tourism pressure, overtourism, saturation, carrying capacity, tourism intensity, resident displacement, neighbourhood burden, impact or attractiveness, and it is never ranked, banded, scored or mapped as a heat surface. The per-1,000-registered-residents figure is a DESCRIPTIVE ratio of two administrative facts with two different periods, not a rate of anything and not a share of dwellings: the denominator is registered residents, never homes or households. Counts belong to the WHOLE OFFICIAL BARRIO and must never be spatially distributed into a circular Lens or any sub-area.

sources.authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid - Censo de Locales
sources.source_period_semantics: Locales and Actividades are the separately fingerprinted nominal September 2026 snapshots approved by Gate F. The conditional resident denominator is a different source and a reference-date stock at 1 January 2026; both dates must remain visible and must never be collapsed to a shared '2026' period.

expected_counts.note: Exactly the canonical CURRENT_131 administrative coverage; no geometry is duplicated in this artifact.

sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING because the application publishes these committed Gate F aggregates as user-facing administrative-area values. Runtime failure is shown explicitly as unavailable, but a malformed, unpinned, mis-joined or semantically incomplete committed artifact must not be deployed.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED FINGERPRINTED ADMINISTRATIVE SNAPSHOT. It is generated only through the reviewed builder, is not refreshed during Pages deployment, and contains no source rows or geometry.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Administratively documented premises in the Censo de Locales under Gate F's exact universes and exclusions. Not verified active or operating businesses, tourism pressure, resident burden, tourism stress, carrying capacity, saturation, overtourism, visitor demand, commercial vitality, accommodation capacity, tourist beds or tourist intensity. Division 55 remains a heterogeneous premises class and is not merged with the separate accommodation catalogue or licensed-VUT source. Values belong to official administrative areas and must never be calculated inside a Lens circle or used in Lens A/B comparison.

sources.authority: Instituto Nacional de Estadistica (INE) - Encuesta de Ocupacion Hotelera
sources.spatial_scope_note: DELIBERATELY NULL. Every other source in this registry is a set of located records or an administrative area, so a bounding box is a meaningful integrity check on it. This source has no coordinates at all: it is one citywide monthly figure for the municipality of Madrid. A spatial envelope would imply a geometry the source does not have. What replaces it is the municipality-code check below.
sources.expected_operation_note: The INE statistical operation this series MUST come from: Encuesta de Ocupacion Hotelera. Operation identity is the central protection against the operation-239 name collision described in series_codes below, so the committed sidecar's declared statistical_operation is verified against this value at the deployment gate and a disagreement blocks publication.
sources.geography_semantics: The official INE 'punto turistico' named Madrid. INE's own EOH methodology (edition 2025, section 5.12) defines a punto turistico as 'Municipio donde la concentracion de la oferta turistica es significativa' - a MUNICIPALITY - and section 5.13 defines a 'zona turistica' separately as a set of municipalities, so the two cannot be confused. INE's Tempus3 metadata for variable 103 (PUNTOS TURISTICOS) under operation 238 publishes the value 'Madrid' with Codigo 28079, the official municipality code, which is the same code carried by the canonical geography artifact. The figure therefore describes the WHOLE MUNICIPALITY and no part of it: not a district, not a barrio, not a Lens circle.
sources.source_period_semantics: Each observation describes a CALENDAR MONTH, and the artifact stores that month as its period. Four different dates exist around this artifact and are never collapsed into one. (1) The month an observation describes. (2) Whether that month is Definitivo or Provisional, which the source publishes per observation as FK_TipoDato and which this project stores as 'status'; months of the current statistical year are provisional and are revised later. (3) INE's publication calendar - the methodology states provisional results for a reference month appear around day 23 of the following month. (4) The builder's retrieved_at clock, which is when this snapshot was taken and is not a property of the data. The interface shows the OBSERVATION PERIOD prominently and keeps retrieval in the source disclosure.

series_codes.note: Series are selected by CODE and each one's own FK_Operacion is verified to be 238 before use. They are NEVER selected by name: statistical operation 239 (Encuesta de Ocupacion en Apartamentos Turisticos) publishes series with IDENTICAL names through the same tourist-point dimension. EOT2743 (operation 238, hotels) and EOT9411 (operation 239, tourist apartments) are both named 'Nacional. Viajeros. Madrid. Residentes en Espana.' and reported 320,715 and 21,334 for their latest published month. Operation 180 (Indicadores de Rentabilidad del Sector Hotelero) supplies ADR and RevPAR through the same dimension and is likewise excluded.

sources.totals_are_published_not_derived: The travellers and overnight-stays totals are read from source-published series and are NEVER computed by adding the two residence components. The published total and that sum disagree by +/-1 in 32 of 105 traveller periods and 26 of 105 overnight-stay periods, because the publisher rounds each estimate independently, so summing would publish a number the source does not publish. The composition block is the one place the two components are added, because a displayed share must total 100 per cent, and that denominator is documented as the sum of the components rather than the published total.

expected_counts.note: ENGINEERING guardrail against an ingestion collapse, not an analytical threshold. The committed series runs 2018-01 to 2026-08. It grows by one month per publication, so a floor well below the observed length passes legitimate growth and fails a truncated download.

sources.zero_semantics: Scoped to this published series. The source published an explicit 0 for 2020-04, when hotels were closed under the COVID-19 state of alarm, and that zero is a real published observation rather than missing data. It is kept distinct from 2020-05 and 2020-06, which the source published as NULL with the note 'Dato no disponible por cierre debido a crisis COVID19'. A null is never rendered as a zero, never interpolated and never averaged over, and a failure to load or validate this artifact must never be degraded into a zero: the interface abstains instead.
sources.blocks_deployment_note: BLOCKING because the Destination Context surface publishes these figures as user-facing numbers with a year-over-year comparison. A deployment must not publish an official statistic that is missing, mis-parsed, detached from its provenance or - the worst case - drawn from the wrong statistical operation, because the failure mode is a confident wrong number under a correct-looking label rather than a visibly empty panel. The browser degrades gracefully when a runtime fetch fails and shows Destination Context as unavailable while leaving the Area Profile, the Lens metrics, VUT and HATI untouched; that is a separate concern from this gate, which verifies the COMMITTED artifact at publication time.
sources.deployment_source_role: COMMITTED STATISTICAL SNAPSHOT. This artifact is not rebuilt during the Pages deployment (rebuilt_at_deploy is false): deployment validation verifies the committed file, and a successful deployment therefore does NOT mean the publisher was re-queried at deploy time. Refreshing it requires explicitly re-running scripts/build_destination_context.py and reviewing the diff. Nothing about this layer is live data, and the browser never calls the publisher's API at runtime.
sources.interpretation_ceiling: Hotel-sector demand in the municipality of Madrid, as measured by the official INE hotel occupancy survey. 'Travellers' is the survey's viajeros entrados: persons making one or more consecutive overnight stays in the SAME establishment, so a person staying in two hotels is counted twice - it is NOT a count of unique people and NOT a count of visitors to Madrid. 'Overnight stays' is pernoctaciones, each night a traveller is accommodated. This is NOT total tourism demand, NOT all accommodation and NOT all visitors: it excludes tourist apartments, tourist dwellings (VUT), campsites, rural accommodation, day visitors and everyone staying in unpaid or private accommodation. The residence split is the publisher's own 'Residentes en Espana' / 'Residentes en el extranjero', which is PLACE OF RESIDENCE and must never be relabelled as domestic/international tourists, nationality or trip type. It is NOT a measure of tourism pressure, overtourism, saturation, carrying capacity, tourism intensity or attractiveness, it is never ranked, banded or scored, and it carries no explanation of why a figure changed: the product reports the observation and never attributes it to events, weather, prices or policy. The figure belongs to the WHOLE MUNICIPALITY and must never be distributed into a district, a barrio or a Lens circle.
